key_insight: A convolutional information-theoretic model isolates the vortical regions that most causally influence a chosen future aerodynamic quantity, revealing different informative structures before and after gust impingement.
engineering_relevance: This enables flow diagnostics that target the structures driving lift or energy transfer, supporting faster interpretation of transient gust–airfoil interactions in low-Reynolds-number aerodynamics.
method: Decompose each flow snapshot into informative and residual components using future-target relevance.
Use convolutional information-theoretic learning to identify vortical structures linked to a specified future variable.
Compare extracted structures against instantaneous force-element analysis and across different targets (lift and scale-dependent energy transfer).
evidence_signal: In turbulent vortex-gust–airfoil interactions at chord-based Reynolds number 5000, the method highlights vortex cores before impingement and emerging shear layers after separation, matching the expected evolution of force-relevant flow features.
watch_item: The extracted structures depend on the chosen future target and trained data distribution, so generalization to other flow regimes or Reynolds numbers should be validated carefully.
paper_title: Extracting informative vortical structures of turbulent wake-extreme vortex gust interactions with machine learning
